component.name: openExpress
component.summary: Manage your Garmin watch on Linux

description.p: openExpress is an unofficial Linux app for Garmin watches connected with a USB cable. It syncs the watch with Garmin Connect and installs software updates, maps, Connect IQ apps and music.

openExpress to nieoficjalna aplikacja dla Linuksa do zegarków Garmin podłączonych kablem USB. Synchronizuje zegarek z Garmin Connect oraz instaluje aktualizacje oprogramowania, mapy, aplikacje Connect IQ i muzykę.

ul.li: Upload activities, sleep, HRV and other health data to Garmin Connect
Wysyłanie aktywności, snu, HRV i innych danych zdrowotnych do Garmin Connect
Send courses, workouts and apps queued in Garmin Connect to the watch
Przesyłanie na zegarek kursów, treningów i aplikacji z kolejki Garmin Connect
Install watch software updates and free maps such as TopoActive
Instalacja aktualizacji oprogramowania i darmowych map, np. TopoActive
Install, update and remove Connect IQ apps and watch faces
Instalacja, aktualizacja i usuwanie aplikacji oraz tarcz Connect IQ
Copy music, podcasts, audiobooks and playlists
Kopiowanie muzyki, podcastów, audiobooków i playlist
Sync automatically in the background when the watch is connected
Automatyczna synchronizacja w tle po podłączeniu zegarka
No telemetry
Bez telemetrii

description.p: The one-time setup reads the data needed to talk to Garmin's servers from your own copy of the official Garmin Express installer for Windows. openExpress is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Garmin Ltd. Garmin, fēnix, Garmin Connect and Garmin Express are trademarks of Garmin Ltd. or its subsidiaries.

Jednorazowa konfiguracja odczytuje dane potrzebne do komunikacji z serwerami Garmina z Twojej kopii oficjalnego instalatora Garmin Express dla Windows. openExpress nie jest powiązany z Garmin Ltd., nie jest przez nią zatwierdzony ani wspierany. Garmin, fēnix, Garmin Connect i Garmin Express są znakami towarowymi Garmin Ltd. lub jej spółek zależnych.

ul.li: Added: when the Garmin sign-in page stops working, the window says so, offers Try Again and shows the command for signing in without it.

Changed: the log and the problem report now describe the sign-in window's environment (WebKit, graphics, session) and keep a crash trace, to make sign-in problems easier to diagnose. Sign-in tickets never appear in the log.
Fixed: starting the window without a graphical session prints one clear line and exits with an error, instead of a series of warnings.
Changed: tiles on the start page share out the width of the window — three columns where they fit, one full-width column in a narrow window — and stand centred with their headings.

Changed: dates read naturally ("8 min ago", "yesterday, 22:30", "3 days ago") on the tiles, in the last sync and in the server status; the full date is in the tooltip. They update by themselves while the page is open.
Fixed: narrowing the window could leave tiles wider than the window.
Changed: new screenshots, with the start page first.

Changed: plugging in or unplugging another device no longer takes you away from the device or remembered-device view you're on; signing in or out keeps you where you are (signing out on the view of a device from your account returns to the start page).

Changed: the last sync is described plainly — relative time, files found and uploaded, what was already in Garmin Connect, and warnings only when something went wrong. Automatic sync is a switch on the device page.
Added: the Garmin Connect account in Preferences, so you can sign in or out without a device connected.
Changed: the command-line sync output ends with the same summary line as the window.
Changed: device-level FIT files are named "device log".
Fixed: a device unplugged from the list could leave a tile behind that failed to open.
Fixed: device types from the Garmin Connect account are remembered after the ownership check.
Fixed: a stale "could not read" tile could appear after unplugging one of several devices (the list was read twice at once).
Fixed: no second detection right after the window starts when the devices are already listed.

Changed: the start page's navigation decisions are made in one place and logged ("navigation: …" lines); the reason an MTP device could not be opened is logged; the host of a refused device picture is logged.
Internal: the devices plugged in are kept in one store; tests for the start page matrix.
Devices in mass-storage mode, such as the Varia RTL515, now work in the Flatpak: the sandbox can see removable drives under /run/media and /media (new permission, documented in the README).
The command line finds a mass-storage device by itself; --path is only for a folder with no device attached. Commands that do not apply to such a device say so.
The device report tells whether the Flatpak came from the openExpress repository or from a bundle, with its build commit.
The server status popover shows relative times, shows the state only when something is wrong, and then offers Try Again.
A remembered device's page no longer closes by itself shortly after the window starts.
Tiles on the start page have one width in every section and are centred; the info line of a USB drive no longer shows its mount path.
Internal: the start page keeps one list of tiles and one picture store.
Remembered and account-only devices show their picture (or a kind icon) on the device page instead of the app icon.
Devices on the start page are listed in a stable order: connected first, then by name.
The tile icon falls back to the model name when the account gives no device kind (Venu 2 shows a watch).
One busy indicator per task: a spinner until the first progress report, then the progress bar.
A map with a missing file or an invalid checksum says which, has no Install button, and is refused in the dry run too.
Readable names for training status, primary training device and Garmin Coach files in sync summaries; "settings change log" for type 41.
Device pictures are loaded without GdkPixbuf.

description.p: The sign-in page, request headers and the Connect IQ store now follow the system language instead of being fixed to Polish; a language chosen in Preferences takes precedence (reported in #5). While the program waits for Garmin's servers during a sync, the progress bar keeps moving and after a while says that this can take a few minutes.

A failed write over MTP no longer deletes the previous firmware or map file on the device when the copy failed before the device was touched, for example because the device was busy or opened in a file manager. The file is removed only with evidence that it was actually being replaced. Reported in an external review.

ul.li: A start page lists your devices as tiles: those connected now, those seen on this computer before and those on your Garmin account, each with its picture, or an icon of its kind until the picture is known. A section of seven or more devices becomes a list. With exactly one device connected, its page opens straight away; a device that is not connected opens a read-only view.
With several devices connected at once, you choose one on the start page instead of getting an error.
Devices in mass storage mode, such as the Varia RTL515, open in the window of the version from source: their information and software updates. The Flatpak cannot open drives yet and says so.
On the command line, openexpress devices lists the devices seen on this computer, and --forget N forgets one.
openexpress cache shows how much space the cache takes and --clear empties it; the same is in Preferences, under Storage.
About openExpress links to a page where you can support the project (Buy Me a Coffee).

Fixes from an external review: a failed write no longer deletes the previous firmware or map file on the device; a missing or malformed checksum no longer skips the verification of a download; all downloads use HTTPS; names from the device or from Garmin's servers can no longer make files be written outside the backup or cache folders.
Refresh asks Garmin's map and update servers once instead of twice.
On the command line, the plan of a map installation (without --apply) lists the files in the order they are written: smallest first.
Error messages after a network failure no longer include the sign-in ticket.
New folders for settings, data and the log are readable only by their owner.
When the device refuses a map's unlock file, writing it is tried up to six times in all, five seconds apart, as Garmin Express does; if it still fails, the message says what to do.
The state of Garmin's servers says "No connection" when nothing has answered since the last good answer, instead of blaming Garmin's servers.

A refusal from the update and map server, which needs no sign-in, no longer shows as an expired sign-in or a wrong clock; a Connect IQ store refusal caused by the computer's clock shows as a wrong clock.
Checking an uploaded activity now counts in the state of Garmin's servers, and the popover shows the date of an answer from another day when it is opened.
Maps are written to the device smallest first, as Garmin Express does; a file that other maps share is never deleted after a failed write.
Removing a map never deletes files that other installed maps still use.
A map that has been copied or removed shows as waiting until the device is unplugged, and cannot be installed twice.
At the bottom of the side panel, the state of Garmin's servers opens a popover with each service, its server and when it last answered.
The progress bar now moves while maps and software updates download, not only while they are copied to the device.
The last sync is remembered for each device; syncing a second device no longer hides the first one's.
After unplugging the device, the window shows "Connect your device" at once.
The two versions of an update ("23.39 → 23.40") stay on one line.
The log names the updates Garmin offers, and the window is logged as the window.
Unplugging the device right after installing or removing an app is now noticed at once.
Unplugging the device and plugging it in again quickly always loads it anew.

The Flatpak can install, update and remove Connect IQ apps on devices that hide their app folder (e.g. the fēnix 8), over a direct USB connection, with the new --device=usb permission (only the USB device nodes). Installing and removing tested on a fēnix 8.
Without the permission, or with Flatpak older than 1.16, such apps are only queued in Garmin Connect, as before. How to turn the permission off is in the README.
The device page no longer reloads a moment after the window opens: a mount event of the device that is open already is ignored, so every request to Garmin is sent once at start instead of twice.

The log, the terminal output of -v and the log attached to a report also hide addresses other than device and web ones (of local files and network shares, e.g. a USB stick in an error of gio copy) and the name of the system user.
The log records the mount events of the device and what the window decides.
"Last sync": the row and the details count the same way (new files, files already in Connect with how they were recognised, files rejected by Garmin, errors), with correct plural forms.
New files are named by their type (activities, sleep, HRV status, device backup…; others as "other data").
The command line, the window and the notification of the background sync use the same words.
The last sync is saved as numbers, so it is shown in the current language.

Reporting a device: "Open on GitHub" in "Report a Device or Problem" opens the GitHub form with the report filled in and a title with the name of the device. An attached log goes to the clipboard, never into the address. On the command line, "openexpress report" prints an address that does the same.
What -v and the background sync print on the terminal passes the same filter as the log file.
The server's answer shown with -v and an unexpected error are filtered too. An unexpected error is one line; the details are in the log.

Software updates: a system update is recognised by its file as well as by what the server says, which does not always mark it. The Updates page starts with a status: the system update with the installed and the new version, how many other updates there are, or that the software is up to date.
Before a system update is copied, the window and the command line warn to charge the device and not to disconnect it. The question in the window shows both versions and links to the license.
Beta versions that Garmin offers to a device are marked as beta.
After a system update is copied, the Updates page and the command line say that it waits for the device to install it when it is disconnected, instead of saying that the software is up to date.
Installing a system update was tested on an Edge 1050 (beta 33.12).
A shorter description of the "Own maps" group, and new screenshots.
Flatpak: the progress bar now moves while a file is copied to the device (maps, maps of your own, music). Until now it stood still and jumped to the end.
Software updates: a progress bar while an update file is copied to the device, in the window and on the command line.
The project is now described as beta, the README says what is stored on the computer after signing in, and the screenshots are new.

Maps of your own: map files that are not from Garmin (.img, e.g. made from OpenStreetMap data) are listed on the Maps page with the name stored in the file. "Add Map…" in the window and "maps add" on the command line copy one to the device, and it can be removed again. Nothing on the device is ever overwritten, and Garmin's own maps cannot be replaced or removed this way.
The device page has a "Maps" row that says whether maps have updates.
The Maps page has a "Check Again" button.
Music: before copying, the app says which files on the device will be replaced.
The log marks every run of the app, so that runs can be told apart, and its first line says the version and whether it is the Flatpak.
Smaller fixes.

Installing a Connect IQ app no longer leaves a request in your Garmin account when the device has no room for it: the free app slots and the app memory are checked before anything is requested, and a dry run reports the same refusal.
The number of free app slots is the one the device reports, so a slot taken by something the app list does not show is counted (e.g. Venu 2).
A device without maps gets one clear message on the Maps page and from the maps command. A map check that fails is reported as an error and no longer looks like an empty list.
Removing a map the device requires is refused at once, before any file is listed.
Sizes are shown in readable units (kB, MB, GB) in all messages and in the device report, counted like GNOME Files (1 kB = 1000 bytes), so they can look slightly larger than in earlier versions.

Smaller fixes: a map named like its type no longer repeats the name, the Sync button says why it is unavailable while a device is starting, and error messages of the command-line tool come after the output printed before them when the output is redirected.
A device that is not on the signed-in Garmin account now gets its picture too.
Installing "all" updates skips files the device already has, and after every install the app says what to do on the device (it may ask whether to install the update and restart).
A Sync button that cannot be used is grey and says why.
Sizes use the decimal separator of the language of the app.
Tested with a Venu 2, including the installation of software updates.
Fixed: the report dialog added in 0.4.1 stayed in memory after it was closed, and the window could occasionally crash afterwards.
Fixed: files that are already on the device (same size and MD5) are no longer offered as updates, e.g. map support files the device briefly does not list right after it is plugged in.
Update types and their importance are shown with readable, translated names.
The window and the command-line tool warn not to unplug the device while it is in use.
The app keeps a log file of what it does, with rotation. Serial numbers, unit IDs, addresses, tokens, e-mail addresses and file names are filtered out before anything is written.
The device report says where the log is and can attach its filtered end.

Connect IQ apps can be installed, updated and removed on devices that hide their app folder (e.g. fēnix 8) over a direct USB connection; the order of widgets is kept. Version from source only; the Flatpak queues such apps in Garmin Connect.
The order of apps and widgets can be restored from a copy of the app list, which is saved before every change.
Primary training device: shown and set from the window and the command line.
Playlists can be added on the Music page.
Sync checks the upload consent of the Garmin account before uploading; the --include-consent option was removed.
The app waits for a device that is still starting after it is plugged in.
Devices that report a name over USB (e.g. Edge 1050) are now detected.
The Music page and the music command show only what the device supports.
Messages say "device" instead of "watch"; the files command counts every file once.

description.p: Sync and Connect IQ now refuse a watch that is not registered to the signed-in Garmin account.
Fixes "Operation not supported" when writing courses, workouts, maps, apps or music to the watch from the Flatpak.
The window opens without flickering: the watch picture is shown at once from the cache instead of being downloaded every time.
The window remembers its size and whether it was maximized.
Fixes "not authorized (HTTP 401)" when uploading new activities.
New "Report a Device or Problem" window and openexpress report command: a report for GitHub without serial numbers or other identifiers.
Reliability release with about 50 fixes from a code review, among others:

ul.li: A damaged activity file no longer stops every sync
Temporary server or network errors no longer lose data; files are retried
Failed writes of software, maps or apps are removed from the watch
Backups never delete the newest backup or unrelated folders
The window cannot be closed while files are being written to the watch
New layout with a sidebar that adapts to narrow windows
Watch overview with a picture of the watch, storage, last sync and software status
Preferences window, keyboard shortcuts and a banner when you are not logged in
Search for maps and built-in activities, Connect IQ app icons

description.p: Running openExpress without a command opens the application window.

ul.li: Flatpak package
Background sync can be turned on in the window
